findings.reason: as written, §5 lands a change that turns `main` red in a test the node may not edit, and the node's own gate cannot report it.
findings.text: §5 instructs the node to register one new refusal family in `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES`, but `tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py:91` asserts `set(DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES) == {f"D{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 25)}` and `CONVERTED_REFUSAL_FAMILIES` is the same frozen range, so a 25th family fails that test, and the file is absent from §5's declared write paths while its scoped gate cannot see it — measured at revision 276444427d: the census test passes (36 passed), and with `D25` added to the dict `set(dict) == expected` becomes False while `crew_run_commands.py` is not in `REFUSAL_SOURCE_PATHS` either

findings.reason: the lock exclusion is a separate defect with its own base-revision control, and splitting it gives each half a gate that can close on one verdict instead of a five-file node proving neither cleanly.
findings.text: §6 bundles the pending-landing marking/repair with an unrelated defect fix (a non-blocking `_pointer_lock` and a resume that takes the promotion lock first), so a §6 that marks and repairs correctly but never lands the lock change still reads as a partial pass on the same verdict

findings.reason: the requirement §5 introduces is precisely that an unreachable remote and a missing branch are distinct answers, so the section that consumes it must be able to show a guard that conflates them fails.
findings.text: §7's third and fourth cases (an unreachable remote declines; a reachable remote with no primary ref declines) carry no negative control, unlike the identical pair in §5 which each carry one ("with a negative control in which reading that empty answer as promotable promotes it")

findings.reason: both sections are done and no future node builds from their line numbers, but a reader following §3's pointers lands in the ledger error handler instead of the release path.
findings.text: §1 cites the withheld refusal at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` near lines 3380–3389 but the string "the reviewed head landed and was pushed, but the worktree was withheld" is at line 3564, and §3's guard/merge/release citations at 3312/3337 name unrelated code while those steps live at 3320 (`_land_a_promoted_run`), the merge confirm mid-function and 3505 (`_release_after_promotion`)

findings.reason: the repair landed under §3 (`_record_release_on_ledger` takes the post-merge reading under `--land`) and no node builds from §1's narrative sentence, so correcting it changes no dispatch.
findings.text: §1 states "the merge and push were confirmed each time; only the release's judgement of the worktree is wrong", while the comment closing §3 records the cause of the same withheld refusal as the pre-merge release record that the post-merge release could not replace, which makes the recorded reason stale rather than the judgement wrong

findings.reason: §2 is done and each of its four cases is listed with its control immediately beside it, so the miscount misleads only a reader counting controls rather than reading them.
findings.text: §2's done-when says "shows three things" and "Three negative controls, one per case" while enumerating four cases and four controls, so a reader cannot tell which case the third control is claimed to cover

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §5, §6 and §7's anchors all resolve (`_remote_head` at `merge.py:614`, `_is_ancestor` at 623, `_port22_refused`/`_port443_env` at 634/644, `_push_and_confirm` at 664–686, `finish_pending_landings` at `pending_landing.py:185` with the live-pointer skip at 233, `_pointer_lock` at `runs.py:453`, `promotion_module.complete` at `recovery_review_acceptance.py:348`), but §1's and §3's line numbers name the wrong code: the withheld refusal is at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3564`, not "near lines 3380–3389", and §3's 3312/3337 name the ledger error handler and unrelated lines while the guard, merge and release live at 3320 (`_land_a_promoted_run`) and 3505.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's gate is scoped to "test files importing `reckon.crew_run_commands` or `reckon.crew.promotion`", which cannot see `tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py`, the test its new refusal family is guaranteed to turn red.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's evidence note sits at `docs/evidence/fragments/a-landing-is-on-main-when-it-says-so/the-withheld-release-cause.html` and §5/§6/§7 gate logs are under the crew run directory; no node writes to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section prose carries no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code; `D24` is a product refusal family that exists in `reckon/crew/refusals.py:95`, not a plan identifier.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's stated root cause ("only the release's judgement of the worktree is wrong") is contradicted by the cause §3 landed on the same refusal family, a stale pre-merge release record rather than a wrong judgement; every other section's mechanism reaches its done-when on a named caller, and §6's repair path is confirmed by `pending_landing.py` lines 309–312 already unlinking a marked pointer after a landing.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §6 carries two independent deliverables: the pending-landing repair marking, and the promotion/resume lock exclusion (`runs._pointer_lock` non-blocking mode plus a reordered resume), each with its own negative control.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every declared relationship resolves: `plan-section-depends-on` wires s6→s5 and s7→s5, both to sections that exist, and §7's dependence on §5 is real because §7's deliverable calls the function §5 adds to `reckon/crew/merge.py` while §7's write paths correctly exclude `merge.py`; §5's placement of the refusal outside `merge.require_promotable_head` is also correct, since that guard is the one `crew merge --run` reaches at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:322`.
